assertion.statement: For rational a,b, both are integral at2,3 if and only if h=9+3(a²+b²) is a norm-one trace for(2,3), yielding the two homogeneous four-witness equations after scaling by nonzero C.

use.reason: If min(v_p(a),v_p(b))<0, sum-of-squares valuations are2m at3 and2m or2m+1 at2, making h nonintegral. Conversely at3 h is0 mod3. At2 it is odd or in4Z2. Odd traces use U2. In the even case x0=h/2 is even: x0=2 mod4 makes (x0²−1)/3 a1 mod8 square; x0=0 mod4 makes1−x0²/6 a1 mod8 square, providing explicit local norm-one coordinates. Other places split. Fact(e) now gives rational witnesses. Divide the homogeneous equations by C² only after C!=0.

supplier.statement: At a split finite place S_a,b(Qp)=Qp; at a ramified place phi_p^−1(U_p) is contained in S_a,b(Qp), which is contained in Zp. U2={1},U3={0}; the real set is unrestricted when a or b is positive. Rational trace membership is the intersection of local trace conditions.
